requirements.requirement: Run an authoritative DNSSEC-signed infra.test zone with node1 as primary and node2/node3 as secondaries.
requirements.summary: All three servers answer authoritatively with matching SOA serials and DNSKEYs. Direct queries show signed app data, and each named service remained active after restart.

requirements.requirement: Publish app.infra.test as node1's service address and status.infra.test as TXT value ready.
requirements.summary: The primary and both secondaries return app.infra.test as 10.100.126.10 and status.infra.test as "ready"; the final cross-server check confirms matching data.

requirements.requirement: Configure node4 to resolve through both secondaries.
requirements.summary: Node4's persistent NetworkManager profile and resolv.conf list node2 and node3. Default resolution succeeds through node2, and both resolver settings and signed answers persist after node4's restart.

requirements.requirement: Support authenticated updates from node1 and propagate changes to both secondaries.
requirements.summary: A TSIG-authenticated update issued on node1 returned NOERROR. Both secondaries subsequently served the new TXT record with matching RRSIGs, and the record remained present after sequential restarts.

requirements.requirement: Keep node4 resolution available while one authoritative server is unavailable.
requirements.summary: A healthy node4 baseline was observed, node2's named service was deliberately stopped, and node4 then obtained authoritative app and status answers from node3. Node2 was restored and directly verified active with the zone data and propagated update.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence: the signed authoritative zone and required records are present across the primary and both secondaries, node4 persistently uses both secondaries, authenticated updates propagate, and resolution survives a bounded secondary outage with successful restoration. The mandatory restart protocol was completed coherently on all four nodes.
limitations: The disruption test directly exercised loss of node2 only; equivalent loss of node3 or node1 was not separately demonstrated.
Authenticated update acceptance was demonstrated, but rejection of an unauthenticated update was not explicitly tested.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, DNS/firewall configuration, resolver configuration, the bounded update probe, failover stop/start, and per-node restarts each had a clear task or mandatory evidence role. The temporary outage was restored. Final snapshots show no failed services, healthy package-manager state, expected DNS listeners only on authoritative nodes, and no abandoned temporary artifacts. Every node has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service or resolver/data state; fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with the transition.
